primary_sources: Tech Domain Selection & Career Choice Methodologies

rules.rule_name: Ikigai-Based Alignment (Intersection of Passion, Skill, and Market Demand)
rules.explanation: Choosing a career path purely based on short-term monetary trends without evaluating personal strengths and genuine interest leads to burnout and career stagnation.
rules.do: Evaluate potential engineering domains (e.g., Embedded Systems, AI, Web, Mobile) by finding the intersection of what you love doing, what you excel at, and what the market actively values.
rules.dont: Do not choose a career path solely because it is trendy if it completely misaligns with your natural aptitudes and long-term interests.

rules.explanation: Committing to a multi-year career track without testing small prototypes or introductory projects in that domain risks investing time in a mismatched path.
rules.do: Build a small, self-contained proof-of-concept project or complete a foundational module in a target domain before fully committing to its career roadmap.
rules.dont: Do not select a major career path based purely on theoretical course descriptions or high-level overviews without hands-on testing.

rules.explanation: Ignoring macroeconomic trends, automation risks, and emerging industrial shifts can lead an engineer into declining legacy domains.
rules.do: Analyze industry growth reports, job board demands, and technological shifts (e.g., AI integration, cloud-native transformation) when selecting a specialization.
rules.dont: Do not choose declining technical stacks or isolated specializations that lack cross-industry applicability.

rules.rule_name: Core Values and Lifestyle Preference Integration
rules.explanation: Disregarding personal lifestyle constraints, remote work preferences, or geographical market dynamics creates friction between your job and personal well-being.
rules.do: Factor in your preferred working environment (e.g., remote vs. on-site hardware labs, fast-paced startups vs. stable enterprises) when finalizing your career direction.
rules.dont: Do not ignore your personal work-style preferences and environmental requirements during the career selection process.
